url: synthetic robots.txt fixture (pattern observed live on github.com/robots.txt style multi-agent blocks)
symptom: For a robots.txt group with multiple consecutive 'User-agent:' lines sharing one rule set (e.g. 'User-agent: GPTBot\nUser-agent: ClaudeBot\nDisallow: /'), parseRobotsTxt created a spurious intermediate block ({agents:['gptbot'], rules:[]}) in addition to the correct combined block ({agents:['gptbot','claudebot'], rules:[disallow /]}). resolveBotStatus's .find() picked the first (empty-rules) match and reported GPTBot as 'allowed' when the real robots.txt disallows it.
classification: clearly-wrong-extraction, caught by unit test before ever reaching production data
fix: packages/scanner/src/extractors/crawlerAccess.ts: parseRobotsTxt rewritten to a simple two-phase state machine (collect agents, then collect rules; a User-agent line seen after a rule line starts a fresh group) instead of a lookup-or-create-block approach that could fork the same agent across two blocks.
regression_check: test/crawlerAccess.test.ts > 'groups multiple consecutive User-agent lines sharing one rule set' pins this exact shape. Full scanner test suite and full corpus re-run after the fix; bot-blocking corpus entry (nytimes.com, which itself only uses single-agent-per-block groups) was unaffected.
